Hi team — quick panel debrief from this morning's interview (45 min). High-level notes and recommendation:

Summary:
- Interview flow: quick intro (5m) + project walkthrough (Maya, 7m) + system-design + production questions (30m)
- Candidate was articulate, solid infra instincts, good at latency tradeoffs.

Strengths:
- Clear ownership of end-to-end inference pipelines and a pragmatic approach to batching/kv-cache tradeoffs.
- Hands-on with model quantization experiments and able to cite concrete perf numbers from previous work.
- Communication: concise and structured answers under pressure.

Risks / concerns:
- Limited exposure to large-scale distributed scheduler internals (some gaps vs our L4 bar).
- Took longer on one deep low-level C++ memory question than expected (still answered but needed hints).

Recommendation: move to a short take-home assignment focused on serving design (2–3 hours) to validate depth on scheduler integration and low-level debugging. If she does well on the take-home, move to an onsite (final) loop.

Next steps for Priyom: send the take-home prompt (I can draft one), ask Scoutline to confirm candidate acceptance, and set a target completion window (72 hours).
